dialogue_history.sentences_no_utterance_types: Tough reforms are justified because endless welfare keeps people stuck in poverty, preventing them from building real skills and independence in this tough economy. Without pushing self-reliance, we're just propping up a broken system that costs taxpayers billions while doing little to fix the root causes. My last point about dependency and resource drain stands firm, as the data shows welfare traps far more than it lifts, so reforms are essential to get people contributing again. Why do you claim that tough welfare reforms leave families in despair when evidence from past changes shows many people moving into work and gaining independence? Focusing on punishment through strict conditions isn't about despair; it's about enforcing accountability to give families real opportunities for self-sufficiency. Justifying reforms means recognising that short-term hardship beats lifelong dependency; a challenging economy demands we cut the safety net's strings to encourage self-sufficiency and reduce the tax burden on everyone else. Many survive on welfare now, but without reforms, we're just propping up a broken system that costs billions and discourages work, so we must push for training and incentives to get folks off benefits.
